taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Solidago radula and lists Texas in its native range.
look_here_first: Touch and inspect the stem and leaves first: rough goldenrod is genuinely scabrous, with short stiff hairs on the stem and rough leaf surfaces. Then compare the broader lower leaves, rapid reduction upward, and the compact terminal panicle.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Burnet — UT PRC Vascular Plants of Burnet County. Travis — UT PRC herbarium specimen index. Williamson — UT PRC Studies on the Vascular Plants of Williamson County. These three exact counties meet the project threshold.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Use exact county floristic or herbarium evidence; do not infer a county from a city or locality label when the county is not explicit.

best_field_traits: stem conspicuously rough or hispid with stiff short hairs
foliage distinctly scabrous to the touch
lower leaves broader and larger, with upper leaves abruptly smaller
terminal compact paniclelike array of many small yellow heads
typical of calcareous rocky openings, prairies, and dry woods
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Solidago radula is the rough/scabrous one: stiff stem and leaf hairs are more tactile and obvious than the fine gray pubescence of S. nemoralis. Its flowering array is generally more compact and terminal.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Rough goldenrod has conspicuously stiff, scabrous stems and leaves plus a compact terminal flowering array; S. nemoralis is grayer and finer-haired with a more one-sided wandlike inflorescence.
